properties.title: Turkey: Activists chant 'shame' as COP31 negotiations falter
properties.summary: Climate activists denounced the proposed outcome of COP31 in Antalya, Turkey, on Friday 20 November 2026, accusing governments of failing to deliver meaningful progress on tackling climate change. They chanted "shame" as negotiations approached their deadline.

properties.title: Germany presses to make Ukraine aid Le Pen-proof
properties.summary: BERLIN — Germany is pushing to lock a durable funding scheme for Ukraine into the EU’s next long-term budget that will be difficult for potential opponents such as Marine Le Pen to veto should she win next year’s French presidential election. Berlin’s plan is to give the EU “headroom”, or financial leeway, to raise additional money for Ukraine beyond the €100 billion the Commission has already proposed, according to a senior European official with knowledge of the negotiations. properties.title: EPP moves to suspend Serbia’s former ruling party
properties.summary: The center-right European People’s Party leadership decided Wednesday to suspend the Serbian Progressive Party, the political home of former Serbian President Aleksandar Vučić. The move comes after the Serbian party, also known as SNS, lost the October 2026 general elections , ousting Vučić, its de facto leader and the country’s president for nine years. properties.summary: The line, which can carry up to 750,000 barrels a day, was shut in 2014 after attacks by the so-called Islamic State terrorist group, and Iraq and Turkey agreed in August on a one-year arrangement for shipments while talks on a longer deal continue.

properties.title: Moldova summons Russia’s envoy over multiple drone incursions
properties.summary: Moldova’s foreign ministry summoned the Kremlin’s ambassador-designate in Chișinău, Oleg Ozerov, on Wednesday morning after Russian drones violated the country’s airspace. Seven drones entered Moldova’s airspace Tuesday afternoon, the country’s defense ministry said , including one over the capital Chișinău. properties.title: Commission takes EU’s Middle East spotlight as Kallas’ Israel channel stays frozen
properties.summary: BRUSSELS — The European Commission is taking a more prominent role in EU diplomacy in the Middle East as Kaja Kallas remains cut off from a direct line of communication with Israel. This week’s schedules put that reality on display: Commission President Ursula von der Leyen and Mediterranean Commissioner Dubravka Šuica are heading to Syria and Jordan, while the EU’s top diplomat hosts a Mediterranean security forum in Brussels.
